title: Habitat comparison table
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Living things and their habitats (Frozen Kingdom)
source: Seeded from science/y6 lesson 13 (Habitat comparison table (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 13: Polar habitats. To understand the conditions in polar habitats and how they differ from habitats near us

questions.q: Name two conditions of the Antarctic.
questions.a: For example: extremely cold, windy, dry, long dark winters.
questions.model: Think about temperature, wind, water and light. Very cold, strong winds. So two conditions: extremely cold and very windy.

questions.q: Which pole is a frozen ocean?
Why are there few plants in the Antarctic?
questions.a: It is too cold, dark and dry; there is little soil.

questions.q: Core: Make a comparison table: Arctic, Antarctic and your local area (temperature, land, plants, animals).
questions.a: Arctic: frozen sea, polar bears, seals; Antarctic: ice continent, penguins, seals; local: mild, woodland animals.
questions.model: Teacher fills the first row: temperature. Arctic: very cold; Antarctic: colder still; local: mild.

questions.q: Extend: Explain why fewer kinds of living things survive in polar habitats.
questions.a: Extreme cold, dark and lack of food and water mean only specially adapted living things survive.

questions.q: Stretch: Why is Antarctica colder than the Arctic?
questions.a: It is high, thick ice on land; the Arctic is ocean, which holds some warmth.

questions.q: Big question: how is the Arctic different from the Antarctic and from where we live?
questions.a: The Arctic is a frozen ocean, the Antarctic an icy continent; both are far colder and darker than our habitats.
